note: relevant_phrases: a chunk counts as relevant if it contains ANY phrase (case-insensitive), so labels survive re-chunking. facts: short strings a correct answer should contain. answerable=false questions have NO support in the document.

questions.question: Which pigment absorbs light for photosynthesis?
questions.reference_answer: Chlorophyll absorbs light, mostly in the red and blue wavelengths.

questions.question: Where in the chloroplast does the Calvin cycle take place?
questions.reference_answer: The Calvin cycle takes place in the stroma of the chloroplast.

questions.question: Which enzyme fixes carbon dioxide onto RuBP?
questions.reference_answer: The enzyme RuBisCO fixes carbon dioxide onto the five-carbon sugar RuBP.

questions.question: Why is ATP called the energy currency of the cell?
questions.reference_answer: ATP is the energy currency of the cell because it stores and transfers usable chemical energy.

questions.question: What is the net ATP gain from glycolysis?
questions.reference_answer: Glycolysis produces a net gain of 2 ATP.

questions.question: In which part of the cell does glycolysis occur?
relevant_phrases: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm
questions.reference_answer: Glycolysis takes place in the cytoplasm.

questions.question: Why are mitochondria called the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.reference_answer: Mitochondria produce most of the cell's ATP through oxidative phosphorylation on the inner membrane.

questions.question: What does lactic acid fermentation do in muscle cells?
questions.reference_answer: It regenerates NAD+ so glycolysis can continue, yielding only 2 ATP per glucose.

questions.question: What does yeast produce during alcoholic fermentation?
relevant_phrases: Alcoholic fermentation in yeast produces ethanol
questions.reference_answer: Yeast produces ethanol and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: Define osmosis.
questions.reference_answer: Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a selectively permeable membrane from low to high solute concentration.

questions.question: How does active transport differ from diffusion?
questions.reference_answer: Active transport requires energy in the form of ATP to move substances against their concentration gradient.

questions.question: What is the overall equation for photosynthesis?
questions.reference_answer: 6CO2 + 6H2O + light energy -> C6H12O6 + 6O2.

questions.question: Which factors affect the rate of photosynthesis?
questions.reference_answer: Light intensity, temperature and carbon dioxide concentration.

questions.question: What is the ten percent rule?
questions.reference_answer: Roughly 10 percent of the energy at one trophic level is passed to the next; the rest is lost as heat.

questions.question: Which plants open their stomata only at night?
questions.reference_answer: CAM plants such as cacti open stomata only at night to save water.

questions.question: How much energy is released when ATP is hydrolysed?
questions.reference_answer: About 30.5 kilojoules per mole.

questions.question: What do helicase and DNA polymerase do during replication?
questions.reference_answer: Helicase unwinds the helix and DNA polymerase adds nucleotides.

questions.question: What are the stages of mitosis in order?
questions.reference_answer: Prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase.

questions.question: How do desert plants avoid losing water yet still fix carbon?
questions.reference_answer: CAM plants open their stomata only at night and store carbon dioxide as organic acids for daytime use.

questions.question: What happens to energy as it moves up a food chain?
questions.reference_answer: Only about 10 percent is passed to the next level; the remainder is lost as heat.

questions.question: How do cells keep making energy when there is no oxygen?
relevant_phrases: When oxygen is absent, cells rely on fermentation
questions.reference_answer: They rely on fermentation.
